headline: Brightline restarts Orlando–West Palm Beach trains Nov 5 after flood closure that began Nov 2
players: Brightline resumed regular Orlando–West Palm Beach service on Thursday, Nov 5. The route had been closed since Monday because of high water in Brevard County, and the suspension was extended to 2 p.m. Wednesday. Service resumed after water receded, repairs were done and Florida East Coast Railway cleared the tracks, signals and crossings. West Palm Beach–Miami ran throughout. No revenue impact was disclosed.
why_it_matters: A roughly three-day outage on the Orlando leg is small against a full year, and no financial impact has been given. The point is weather exposure on a shared corridor with a single route to Orlando, which matters for insurance, reliability and ridership assumptions. Still open: the bond restructuring and the Miami-Dade commuter contract talks.
why_you_care: This is the asset you underwrote at Rothschild; a clean three-day recovery eases the immediate operating worry, but the corridor's flood risk belongs in any updated view of Brightline's downside.

headline: FERC clears MARA's purchase of Long Ridge from FTAI Infrastructure; deal not yet closed, MARA expects close in coming weeks
players: MARA said on Nov 5 that FERC found its purchase of Long Ridge Energy & Power from FTAI Infrastructure consistent with the public interest. The April 30 agreement values Long Ridge at about $1.52bn before closing adjustments; it covers a 505 MW combined-cycle gas plant in Hannibal, Ohio and 1,600+ acres. Mugglehead reports at least $785m of debt is assumed. FTAI Infrastructure reports Q3 after the close on Nov 5, with a call on Nov 6 at 8:00 a.m. ET.
why_it_matters: The price works out to roughly $3m per MW of nameplate capacity (my arithmetic on the headline value, debt included). The buyer is a bitcoin miner moving into AI compute, so the upside rests on signing a tenant for the campus, and MARA still lists financing as a risk. FIP says it will use net proceeds to repay corporate debt. Watch the close, any tenant lease, and what is left at FIP.
why_you_care: Your old FTAI Infrastructure situation just cleared its main regulatory hurdle; the Long Ridge price is a live gas-plus-land comp, and FIP's remaining assets are worth flagging to MSIP as angles.

headline: Tracker counts 69 large US data-centre projects cancelled since 2024; 39 withdrawn by developers, 27 denied by governments
players: A Programs.com tracker updated Nov 4 lists 69 US projects of at least 100 MW or $1bn that were withdrawn, denied or lost their land deal since January 2024, across 26 states. Of these, 39 were withdrawn by the developer, 27 were denied by a local or state government, and 3 ended over a land or utility deal. The counts and criteria are the site's own, not an official dataset.
why_it_matters: Most infrastructure underwriting of AI power assumes announced data-centre load turns into real demand. Local denials and developer withdrawals are the clearest sign that some of it will not. For a gas plant or powered-land deal, that argues for contracts with take-or-pay terms and creditworthy tenants rather than pipeline megawatts. Treat the tracker as directional until checked against primary sources.
why_you_care: It is a risk check for any data-centre power or powered-land deal MSIP looks at, including comps like Long Ridge, where the tenant is not yet signed.

headline: RBC: TransAlta's proposed Alberta data-centre deal would start at 230 MW from existing gas plants, scalable to 1,600 MW
players: RBC says TransAlta's proposed Boreal Technology Hub agreement would start with 230 MW supplied from existing gas-fired plants and could reach 1,600 MW, with Sundance Unit 5 and Keephills Unit 1 upgrades as longer-term options. Management is aiming to finalise it in early 2027. RBC also points to the Alberta Electric System Operator updating market rules, including clearer 'phase 2A' rules. This is an analyst view of a proposed deal, not a signed contract.
why_it_matters: The idea is to turn existing gas plants into long-term contracted supply for always-on data-centre load, which supports steadier cash flows than selling at market prices. RBC's point is that contract terms matter as much as power prices. Watch the AESO rule changes, the contract length and pricing, and whether the deal is finalised in early 2027.
why_you_care: A Canadian comp for pairing existing gas generation with data-centre contracts; the contract term and rule changes are the underwriting risks to track.

headline: Odfjell SE reports Q3 2026 today; terminals were a small part of group earnings last year
players: Odfjell SE scheduled its third-quarter 2026 report for Nov 4, and its site shows a results presentation posted on Nov 3. I did not retrieve the Q3 figures. In the fourth quarter of 2025, Odfjell Terminals contributed a net result of $1.8m, against $2.6m in 3Q25. The terminals business covers Houston and Charleston in the US, as well as sites in Korea and Belgium.
why_it_matters: The group is mainly a chemical tanker business, so terminal profit is a small slice and the terminal story is easy to miss. Houston and Charleston occupancy and any commentary on specialty chemical storage demand are what to read for. Check the report for terminal earnings, capex and any portfolio moves.
why_you_care: Your old deal: read the terminals section of today's report for occupancy and earnings trend; there is nothing yet to flag at MSIP.

headline: Drax, Brookfield and Radiant announce partnership for 1 GW+ AI data centre at Drax Power Station; first phase 100 MW by 2028
players: Drax, Brookfield and Brookfield's UK AI platform Radiant announced the partnership on 3 November. Drax supplies land, power and its 4 GW grid connection. Brookfield supplies capital through its joint venture with Qatar's Qai, starting with £2.5bn for phase one. Total spend could pass £20bn, including chips. Phase one is up to 100 MW, targeted for Q1 2028, with a further 500 MW by 2031. Drax shares rose over 8% to 878p.
why_it_matters: The scarce asset is the grid connection, not the building. Drax brings a 4 GW connection and 2.6 GW of dispatchable generation, which skips years of queue time. Brookfield funds it through a Qatar-backed joint venture. Phase one still needs planning and regulatory approval, commercial agreements and a customer, so a signed tenant is the next thing to watch.
why_you_care: A live comp for turning an existing power site into AI capacity; MSIP's Flexential stake is its closest digital holding, so a connection-first premium is worth marking against.

headline: I Squared closes ISQ Global Infrastructure Credit Fund II above $2.4bn; $3bn including co-investment vehicles
players: I Squared announced the final close of ISQ Global Infrastructure Credit Fund II at more than $2.4bn, over four times its predecessor. Including co-investment vehicles, commitments reach $3bn, twice the initial target. The fund has already committed about 37% of its capital; Bloomberg says investors include insurers, sovereign wealth funds and pensions in the US and overseas. Latham & Watkins advised I Squared.
why_it_matters: Private infrastructure credit is becoming a bigger source of financing for power, data centres and other large projects, which gives sponsors another place to borrow besides banks and bonds. A fund already about 37% committed points to a steady deal flow. Watch whether I Squared pairs this credit with its own equity deals, and what pricing lenders accept.
why_you_care: I Squared can now offer capital across the structure; keep that in mind when MSIP bids against it, and use its credit deals as financing comps.

headline: Tianjin Port Holdings agrees to buy two terminal operators from parent for RMB6.224bn (about $932m)
players: Shanghai-listed Tianjin Port Holdings agreed to buy full ownership of Tianjin Port Second Container Terminal for RMB3.865bn ($579m) and Tianjin Port Huisheng Terminal for RMB2.359bn ($353m) from its parent, Tianjin Port Group. A supplementary agreement was signed on 22 October 2026. Both operators become wholly owned subsidiaries, and the company warns completion is not guaranteed.
why_it_matters: This is a parent injecting assets into its listed arm, not an arm's-length sale, so the prices are a weak comp. It does show state port groups consolidating container and bulk terminals into one listed vehicle. The source gives no earnings figures, so no multiple can be worked out. Watch for the valuation basis in the shareholder circular.
why_you_care: Background only: a China port consolidation with no sponsor involved and no direct read-across to MSIP or to the LOGISTEC/Termont thesis.

headline: AllianzGI closes Infrastructure Credit Opportunities Fund II at €1.5bn, above its €1bn target
players: Allianz Global Investors held the final close of AICOF II with €1.5bn of commitments from institutional investors in Europe and Asia. The fund launched in June 2024, held a first close of €533m in December 2024 and reached €1bn at its third close in February 2026. Allianz says it can invest across sectors and different parts of the capital structure.
why_it_matters: Another infrastructure debt fund closing 50% above target shows lender capital is plentiful. For equity sponsors that means more room to finance acquisitions and refinance with flexible, subordinated or holdco debt, which supports bid prices. Watch whether debt funds start to compete with banks on pricing for contracted, mid-risk assets.
why_you_care: Background for underwriting: plentiful infrastructure credit supports leverage assumptions in MSIP models, alongside the I Squared credit close the same day.

headline: I Squared, ADIA subsidiary and Avolon agree to launch Constellation Aviation with 22-aircraft, $1.4bn seed portfolio
players: I Squared Capital and a wholly owned ADIA subsidiary agreed with Avolon to set up Constellation Aviation. On completion it is expected to buy 22 aircraft from Avolon with a current market value of $1.4bn, average age about five years, on lease to 17 airlines in 15 countries. Avolon keeps a minority stake and is exclusive manager and servicer; a bank-syndicated debt facility supports it, the deal needs regulatory approvals, and financial terms were not disclosed. Reuters, via a source, says the partners plan to grow it to as much as $6bn.
why_it_matters: The cash flows are contracted lease income, so value comes from growing the fleet, not from one purchase. Avolon's Boeing and Airbus order books supply new aircraft, which are the scarce input, and its minority stake keeps it aligned. DAE launched similar platforms with Neuberger and Blackstone this year. Watch regulatory sign-off and how fast the $6bn ambition gets funded.
why_you_care: A direct rival is stretching the infrastructure label to aircraft leasing alongside ADIA; treat it as a read on competitor appetite, with no clear overlap with MSIP's stated sectors.

headline: Igneo closes fourth European diversified infrastructure strategy at its €6bn hard cap, six months after first close
players: Igneo Infrastructure Partners closed the fourth vintage of its European Diversified Infrastructure Strategy at its €6bn ($6.7bn) hard cap. The target was €4bn, and commitments came from more than 90 investors across Europe, Asia Pacific and North America. IREI says it is about 11% larger than the previous vintage, which hit its hard cap in October 2025.
why_it_matters: A hard-cap close in six months shows capital is still available to managers with a track record, even though the archive's Infralogic data has nine-month 2026 fundraising 39% below 2025. More dry powder chasing European diversified assets supports pricing for core-plus deals. Watch which managers reach hard cap quickly and which stall.
why_you_care: Fundraising is polarising toward established names, which is the market backdrop for MSIP's own fund raising and for the European core-plus assets you will compete for.

headline: Brightline suspends Orlando–West Palm Beach trains on Nov 2 over flooding in Brevard County; Miami service normal
players: Brightline halted Orlando–West Palm Beach service on Monday night because of high water on the rail corridor in Brevard County. Service was expected to stay suspended until 8:30 p.m. on Nov 3; one outlet said trains to Orlando would be halted until Thursday. Brightline is working with Florida East Coast Railway to inspect tracks, signals and crossings once water recedes; West Palm Beach–Miami runs normally. DeSantis declared a state of emergency in seven counties.
why_it_matters: The Orlando link is the intercity leg that has to carry ridership and fares. A multi-day outage costs revenue and shows how exposed a shared corridor is to extreme weather. The cost is probably small against the restructuring, but watch the restart date, any damage found on inspection and whether bondholder updates mention it.
why_you_care: Your old deal: this is a weather outage, not a change to the thesis, though corridor resilience and insurance are worth flagging if MSIP ever looks at rail.

headline: Stonepeak completes purchase of 65% of Castrol from bp; bp keeps 35%, CPP Investments joins as indirect minority holder
players: Stonepeak closed its purchase of a 65% controlling stake in Castrol from bp, which keeps 35%. The deal was agreed in December 2025 at an enterprise value of about $10.1bn. CPP Investments committed up to $1.05bn as an indirect minority holder. The new board is chaired by Ben van Beurden and has three Stonepeak directors, two from bp and one from CPP. Anthony Borreca of Stonepeak said near-term work will focus on operational improvement.
why_it_matters: Lubricants earn from branded, replacement-driven demand, not a long-term contract, so Stonepeak is underwriting operating improvement and not a fixed yield. Per bp, its retained 35% is not expected to bring earnings or a dividend in the short to medium term. A Spanish outlet reports Stonepeak gets priority on distributions. Watch for a cost programme and any later bp exit.
why_you_care: Stonepeak, at about $98bn AUM, paid roughly $10bn of enterprise value for a consumer-facing industrial carve-out, a useful marker for how big the rival is willing to go outside classic contracted assets.

headline: Aramco closes purchase of 49% of Saudi AI company HUMAIN; PIF keeps 51%; about $2.6bn cash plus AI assets
players: PIF and Aramco announced the closing of a deal in which an Aramco subsidiary takes 49% of HUMAIN, with PIF keeping 51%. Aramco will put in about $2.6bn of cash in 2026, plus AI, compute and digital assets. The companies say it supports HUMAIN's plan to deploy 3 GW of AI data centre capacity by 2030.
why_it_matters: Part of the price is paid in assets, so the $2.6bn cash figure is not a valuation and should not be used as a comp. The point is who is funding AI capacity: state-backed energy groups are now direct owners of compute and data centre build-out. That adds a well-capitalised competitor for sites, power and customers in the Gulf.
why_you_care: Background for digital infrastructure underwriting: strategic and sovereign money is taking big stakes in AI capacity, which can push up entry prices on platforms MSIP might otherwise look at.
